reason: The turning sensors fit the fluid-filled canals, forming one of the two balance organs.
expectation: The sensors will be positioned in the canals to detect head rotation.

effect: The canals now have rotation sensors; the separate tilt and acceleration organs still need assembly.
reaction: The fluid-bending explanation makes the turning connection clear.
reason: The weighted membranes are shown above the hair cells in the otolith organs.
expectation: This should assemble sensors for head tilt and linear acceleration.

effect: The otolith organs are assembled, with weighted gel bending hair bundles during tilt or linear acceleration.
reaction: The comparison between tilt and starting motion clarifies what these sensors detect.
reason: Both balance organs need to connect to the vestibular pathways; I will start with the rotation sensors.
expectation: The rotation sensors should connect to nerve fibres leading toward the brainstem.

alternatives.reason: The two organs might first be assembled together before adding their nerve pathways.

effect: The rotation sensors now connect to nerve endings, with a branch available for the gravity-sensing organs.
reaction: The remaining branch makes the next connection clear.
reason: Connect the other balance organs to the available nerve branch.
expectation: Both sets of balance sensors should connect to pathways toward the brainstem.

effect: Both balance organs now send signals through vestibular nerves to the brainstem.
reaction: The separate receptor fibres make the two inputs easy to distinguish.
reason: The brainstem pathways can connect the balance signals to eye and posture reflexes.
expectation: The balance pathways should connect to eye-movement and postural motor circuits.

effect: The balance organs now connect to brainstem pathways for eye movements and posture; they still need integration with the body.
reaction: The branching pathways make the two reflex destinations clear.
reason: The completed balance pathways belong in the existing body with its brain, eyes and spinal cord.
expectation: The balance organs and their reflex pathways should connect to the existing body.

effect: The balance pathways are integrated into the body: they help steady the eyes during head turns and adjust posture alongside other sensory information. The goal is complete.
reaction: The opposing eye movement makes the purpose of the reflex connection concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Integrating the balance pathways with the body connected the constructed organs to a recognizable function: keeping a view steadier while the head turns.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the reflex pathways was comparatively procedural: the planned picture showed where they branched but did not yet show what the reflexes did.

surprise.text: The weighted membranes respond both to head tilt and to changes in straight-line motion; the comparison distinguished acceleration from steady movement.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the nerve and reflex connections were largely straightforward fittings.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the final connection made the anatomy useful for explaining an everyday experience, and I would be curious to see another system connected this way.
